body:

name: UsageDeck v0.7.15 — OpenCode V2 support
body:
UsageDeck now supports OpenCode V2's default Console sign-in and new local usage storage.

- Reads the active saved OAuth or Go API-key login from OpenCode V2, with no key to copy into UsageDeck.
- Fetches Session, Weekly, and Monthly Go quotas for the selected workspace.
- Reads V2 local token usage and spend, while preserving V1 history without counting migrated sessions twice.
- Respects `OPENCODE_DB` and supports V2 logins in separate OpenCode profile directories.
- Keeps V1 login support. Signing out in V2 does not restore a stale V1 key.
- Includes TLS security fixes and removes unused legacy ZIP updater support.

After updating, refresh the OpenCode card. If OpenCode's OAuth login has expired, open OpenCode to renew it and refresh again.

name: UsageDeck v0.7.14 — Grok Bot usage
body:
## Grok Bot usage in the Grok card

- Track Grok Bot's included weekly allowance and its own reset time alongside regular Grok usage.
- Sign in to the Grok Bot desktop app to enable the meter; a Grok CLI login is optional for Bot-only users.
- See Bot Extra Usage status and the Cursor account's monthly spending cap, plus a direct Bot Usage dashboard link.
- Unified subscriptions show Shared Weekly with an explanation of the Grok, Grok Bot, and Cursor pool.
- Keep the working meter visible if the other product's usage source is temporarily unavailable.

The reader follows the active desktop account and reads its existing encrypted login. It does not rotate the Grok Bot refresh token or overwrite the app's credential files. macOS may ask for access to Grok Bot Safe Storage. If the saved sign-in expires, open Grok Bot, then refresh UsageDeck. Linux native reading supports Electron basic-text and Secret Service storage backends.

Bot Extra Usage is account-level Cursor spending and can include Cursor work. Grok CLI token history remains separate from cloud Bot work. Internal product endpoints may change.

The release also updates quinn-proto to 0.11.18 to resolve five network dependency security advisories.

name: UsageDeck v0.7.13 — z.ai reset account matching
body:
Fixes missing z.ai reset cards when UsageDeck uses a different API key from the one generated by ZCode for the same personal Coding Plan account.

- UsageDeck verifies the subscription owner reported by Z.ai for your saved key and your ZCode login, so you can keep your existing key.
- Different accounts and unavailable or ambiguous ownership remain excluded. The existing exact-key connection still works without the extra verification request.
- Reset counts, expiry dates, and expiry reminders now work with verified alternate keys. Requests remain read-only and do not redeem reset cards.
- Updated setup instructions and all five translations explain the account-verification fallback.

Sign in to ZCode with the same personal Coding Plan account, update UsageDeck, and refresh. **Use ZCode API key** remains available as a fallback when account verification is unavailable; choosing it replaces that card's saved key.

body:
Fixes the missing Claude and z.ai reset inventories.

- Missing or filtered data remains unavailable rather than appearing as a false zero. Older Claude deployments that reject grant queries still show ordinary quotas.

Z.ai reset tracking requires a personal Coding Plan login in ZCode; team/start-plan connections are currently unsupported. Enable **Settings → Notifications → Resets expiring** to receive expiry reminders.

name: UsageDeck 0.7.10
body:
UsageDeck 0.7.10 improves Claude credential access on macOS and includes the fixes merged since 0.7.9.

## What's changed

- Read Claude Code credentials through the same Apple-signed Keychain reader used by the CLI, reducing repeated permission prompts naming UsageDeck when Claude renews its login.
- Distinguish inaccessible or incomplete Claude Code credentials from a Desktop-only login, with accurate recovery instructions.
- Detect Claude logins without requesting access to credential secrets during startup discovery.
- Include recent improvements to localized UI text, refresh handling, provider robustness, and dependencies.

## Updating

If Claude Code's saved access and refresh tokens have been cleared, run `claude`, use `/login`, then refresh UsageDeck. Granting Keychain access alone cannot restore missing tokens. Claude Code continues to renew its own Keychain login; UsageDeck does not change that item's access controls.

The macOS Universal app is Developer ID signed and notarized. Downloads also include Windows x64/ARM64 installers and Linux x64/ARM64 AppImage, Debian, and RPM packages. Automatic updates are cryptographically signed; Linux in-app updates use AppImage builds.

name: UsageDeck 0.7.7
body:
UsageDeck desktop release for Windows and Linux on x64/ARM64, plus a macOS Universal build.

This release stops UsageDeck from provoking macOS Keychain password prompts, gives OpenCode one card per login, and makes kickstart renew the account its card actually tracks.

### New

- **One card per OpenCode login.** Everything an OpenCode account needs — its `opencode-go` credential and its usage databases — lives in one data directory, so sibling directories following the `opencode-<name>` convention next to the default directory are treated as separate logins, the same shape alternate `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`s already have for Claude. A sibling is admitted only when it holds a subscribed `opencode-go` login; the default directory and keyless siblings stay a single card. Each account scans only its own databases and resolves its own cached snapshots. No credential ever passes through UsageDeck.

- **Account-aware kickstart, and a circuit breaker.** A scoped Claude account's built-in kickstart now sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so the prompt renews the login the card is watching. Previously it silently renewed the default account while the evaluator watched a different one's windows — paying for a kick on every cooldown that could never satisfy the check. Auto-kickstart also stops after two consecutive kicks fail to open the scoped window (a command targeting the wrong account, a plan that never reports the window), announcing the suspension in the log instead of prompting every thirty minutes forever.

### Fixed

- **macOS no longer asks for your login keychain password after a refresh.** Two separate faults, both in how UsageDeck wrote provider-owned credentials. It could create an item that was missing, and an item created that way carries an access control trusting only UsageDeck — locking the owning CLI out of its own login. It also wrote through an API that rewrites an existing item's access control to trust only the calling process, which evicted the owner's own reader (`/usr/bin/security` for Claude Code) and made every later read block on SecurityAgent. Writes are now update-only and modify the data in place, leaving the access control untouched.

- **macOS folder-access prompts during Claude account discovery.** Discovery enumerated every dot-directory in your home folder and tried to open a marker file inside each one — including `~/.Trash` and iCloud's Mobile Documents — which macOS bills to UsageDeck as consent prompts for folders it has no business touching. Candidates now have to follow the `.claude` naming convention.

- **Kimi's weekly window disappearing on over-quota accounts.** Kimi reports a negative remaining once you are over quota, which the parser rejected before falling back to a field the current API no longer returns — dropping the weekly window entirely, the same regression 0.7.5 fixed. Negative remaining now clamps to a fully-used window.

- **OpenCode discovery aborting startup.** A sibling directory symlinking another sibling resolved to the same path and produced two runtimes claiming one provider id, which the registry rejects — taking the whole app down on launch. Discovery now skips alias entries and excludes the default directory by canonical path, so a symlinked default is no longer counted twice with double the usage.

- **Kickstart environment being overridden by your login profile.** Account-scoped variables were set on the spawned shell, so a login profile could overwrite `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` before `exec` ran and renew the wrong login — the exact failure the environment support existed to prevent. The exports now live inside the script with shell-quoted values.

- **Discovered account cards landing far from their provider.** A newly discovered `opencode@` account was inserted after every unrelated provider on upgraded installs; any account-shaped id now sits with the rest of its family.

- **The Linux tray staying off for the whole session.** A single launch-time probe concluded no tray was available whenever the status notifier watcher had not yet claimed its D-Bus name. Detection now probes a second time after a bounded wait; tray-less sessions pay at most one extra three-second pause, once.

- **Mixed-language scope labels.** The scope selector composed English connectives around translated window names in four locales, and named the window "weekly" regardless of what the provider actually rolls. The full phrases are now translated, and the labels derive from the provider's own window list.

### Notes

- OpenCode account cards appear after a restart, alongside the base card.
- CommandCode's built-in kickstart is withheld on Windows, where `cmd` resolves to `cmd.exe` inside the kick shell and would spend the whole timeout spawning a nested shell.
- Z.ai legacy plans (for example Coding Lite) still do not report a weekly window; keep the scope on "Session" there.

### Internal

- The keychain integration jobs now run the whole credential-store module rather than one named test, so tests added alongside a keychain change are actually exercised on real platform stores.
- The Linux X11 tray smoke retries once on a lost D-Bus registration race, and two order-dependent test flakes were fixed.

Automatic updates are cryptographically signed. Linux in-app updates are supported by AppImage builds; Debian packages update through the package installer.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/lamchun1110/UsageDeck/compare/v0.7.6...v0.7.7

name: UsageDeck 0.7.6
body:
UsageDeck desktop release for Windows and Linux on x64/ARM64, plus a macOS Universal build.

This release extends kickstart window scopes to Codex, Z.ai, and CommandCode, gives CommandCode a built-in kickstart, and moves the build pipeline to Node 24 LTS.

### New

- **Kickstart window scopes for Codex, Z.ai, and CommandCode.** The weekly windows of all three re-anchor on the first message of the window — verified against live accounts, where the weekly start matched the session start to the same second — so they now offer the same scope selector Kimi got in 0.7.5:
  - **Session only** (default, previous behavior)
  - **Weekly only** — one tiny prompt when the weekly has rolled over, never because the session expired
  - **Session and weekly** — kick when either rolls over

  With Kimi, Codex, Z.ai, and CommandCode covered, a dead weekly window never has to sit idle until your next real message.

- **CommandCode built-in kickstart.** The toggle now works with no custom command: UsageDeck runs `cmd -p Hi --no-session` — non-interactive, and the throwaway prompts stay out of your conversation history.

### Notes

- Z.ai legacy plans (for example Coding Lite) do not report a weekly window; keep the scope on "Session" there.
- OpenCode and MiniMax weeklies reset on a fixed Monday schedule — a prompt cannot restart them, so no scope option is offered for those providers.

### Internal

- CI and release builds moved from Node 22 (maintenance LTS) to Node 24 (active LTS).

name: UsageDeck 0.7.5
body:
UsageDeck desktop release for Windows and Linux on x64/ARM64, plus a macOS Universal build.

This release fixes the Kimi weekly card and adds kickstart window scopes, so a dead weekly window can be restarted automatically.

### Fixed

- **Kimi's weekly quota now displays correctly.** The Kimi API changed shape — it reports the weekly window as `remaining` instead of `used` — so the weekly card showed no data and "Reset unavailable". Both API shapes now map, with usage and the reset countdown restored.

### New

- **Kickstart window scopes.** Kimi's weekly window is first-message rolling, just like its session: once it expires it stays dead until your next message. In Customize → Session Kickstart you can now choose which windows the kickstart renews:
  - **Session only** (default, previous behavior)
  - **Weekly only** — UsageDeck sends one tiny prompt when the weekly has rolled over, and never just because the session expired
  - **Session and weekly** — kick when either rolls over

  The selector appears only for providers with extra rolling windows (currently Kimi, including named accounts).

### Internal

- The Windows build of the v0.7.4 CLI-path probe compiled with an unused constant, which failed the Windows CI lint jobs; the release binaries were unaffected.

name: UsageDeck 0.7.4
body:
UsageDeck desktop release for Windows and Linux on x64/ARM64, plus a macOS Universal build.

This is a fix release: named API-key accounts now work end-to-end, session kickstart is reliable again on Codex and Claude, and a batch of robustness, privacy, and localization fixes landed.

### Named API-key accounts (OpenRouter, Z.ai, Kimi, MiniMax)

- **Fixed:** every named account failed its refreshes with "Provider data does not match its registered metric contract." Accounts now report their own provider id and refresh correctly.
- New accounts appear the moment they are created — no restart needed — and removing an account never leaves a ghost card behind, even when settings reconciliation fails.
- The Add-account picker no longer offers existing accounts as families.
- Account ids are now derived with a stable hash, so they survive app upgrades; accounts created by earlier releases keep working.

### Session kickstart

- **Fixed:** the Codex kickstart failed on every attempt — its pinned `gpt-5-mini` model has been retired by ChatGPT-account Codex. It now uses `gpt-5.6-luna`, the cheapest current tier.
- **Fixed:** the Claude kickstart could not find the `claude` CLI when it was installed under `~/.local/bin`. Built-in CLIs now resolve through your own login shell first, then common install roots — covering every install method your profile exposes.
- Kickstart prompts run in the background, so a manual refresh no longer waits on the CLI to finish.
- Kickstarts are suppressed for providers that are mid-refresh or showing cached data after a failure.

### Refresh reliability

- A refresh racing an account removal can no longer hang the refresh batch.
- A forced refresh queued behind a timed-out provider now runs once the stuck worker drains, instead of being silently dropped.
- Concurrent resyncs cannot regress the provider catalog, and quota-history fetches are deduplicated and cached.

### Security & privacy

- Linux Secret Service calls are capped and deadline-bounded; the macOS keychain probe caches answers and survives wedged searches instead of disabling probing for the session.
- Grok auth entries are excluded from debug logs, password buffers are zeroized after use, and expired rate-limit cooldowns are pruned.
- Notification delivery waits at most ten seconds instead of blocking a refresh worker indefinitely.

### Localization & UI

- The share card is fully localized (no more hardcoded English), countdown durations localize through the message catalogs, and additional screen-reader labels were added.
- Count-format quota readings compact like every other metric.
